claims.claim_text: GPTZero's Hallucination Detector is designed to automatically detect hallucinated sources and poorly supported claims in essays.
claims.evidence_span: GPTZero's Hallucination Detector automatically detects hallucinated sources and poorly supported claims in essays.

claims.claim_text: GPTZero source finder detects checkable objective claims in text and matches them to sources from online, academic, and publicly available data.
claims.evidence_span: Source finder will detect as many checkable, objective claims in your text and match those to sources from online, academic, and publicly available data coming from AI-powered search engines.

claims.claim_text: In the field of artificial intelligence, a hallucination or artificial hallucination is a response generated by AI that contains false or misleading information presented as fact.
claims.evidence_span: In the field of artificial intelligence (AI), a hallucination or artificial hallucination (also called bullshitting, confabulation, delusion, or mirage) is a response generated by AI that contains false or misleading information presented as fact.

claims.claim_text: Symbolic artificial intelligence models generally do not produce hallucinations, unlike large language models.
claims.evidence_span: Symbolic artificial intelligence models generally do not produce hallucinations, unlike large language models.

claims.claim_text: The survey aims to provide an extensive overview of current techniques employed to detect, verify, mitigate, or correct hallucinations in generative AI models.
claims.evidence_span: The present survey aims to provide an extensive overview of current techniques employed to detect, verify, mitigate, or correct hallucinations in generative AI models.

claims.claim_text: Major detection and verification paradigms include retrieval-augmented generation, factuality evaluation metrics, automated fact-checking, and natural language inference.
claims.evidence_span: Subsequently, we examine major detection and verification paradigms, including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), factuality evaluation metrics, automated fact-checking, natural language inference (NLI), knowledge-grounded reasoning, multi-model verification, and self-reflection-based approaches.

claims.claim_text: AI hallucinations are instances where an AI system produces outputs that sound plausible but are factually wrong, irrelevant or entirely fabricated.
claims.evidence_span: AI hallucinations are instances where an AI system produces outputs that sound plausible but are factually wrong, irrelevant or entirely fabricated.

claims.claim_text: Consistency hallucinations occur when an AI model contradicts itself within the same conversation.
claims.evidence_span: Consistency hallucinations occur when an AI model contradicts itself within the same conversation.

claims.claim_text: Stanford research found that even specialized legal AI tools hallucinate between 17% and 34% of the time.
claims.evidence_span: Stanford research found that even specialized legal AI tools hallucinate between 17% and 34% of the time.

claims.claim_text: A 2024 Stanford study found that combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback, and guardrails led to a 96% reduction in hallucinations.
claims.evidence_span: A 2024 Stanford study found that combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), and guardrails led to a 96% reduction in hallucinations.
